title: AI 要跨越盧比孔河了嗎？自我成長的 AI 離我們多遠 (下集)

topic_alignment.paraphrase: The lecturer opens the second lecture and resumes the question of whether AI can improve itself.

The lecturer recalls a conditional scenario in which AI creates more capable AI or improves itself, using technological singularity and humanity's last invention as framing. This is an introductory hypothesis, not evidence that such a threshold has been reached.

The lecture distinguishes the model A_theta, the human-desired target represented in research by L-hat or a benchmark, and the training loss L(A_theta,H). Here H denotes information supplied by humans as a proxy for their goal, including training examples, textbooks or an instruction. It does not denote the agent harness on these pages. The lecturer explicitly notes that real-world goals can be too complex for a single benchmark.

The model parameters are updated by gradient descent on L, producing theta-prime and then replacing theta for another iteration. The lecturer hopes the updated model performs better under L-hat; the slide's lower-loss inequality is an intended outcome, not a mathematical guarantee from descending the proxy loss. The lecture distinguishes lower-is-better loss from higher-is-better reinforcement-learning reward.

The proposer generates questions, the solver solves them, and the verifier judges the answers, allowing an iterative process with almost no human intervention in that loop. The lecturer adds that supplying proposers with textbooks or examples can help in some recent work. The statement does not remove human choices of objectives, initial models, software, evaluation or other setup.

terminology_and_claim_checks.topic: H denotes human-provided goal information on page 3
terminology_and_claim_checks.paraphrase: H is introduced as human-provided information and a proxy for L-hat. This differs from the pedagogical harness H used in chapter 13 and from the harness notation introduced after this chapter's page range.
Training data, textbooks and an instruction such as improving at mathematics are examples of the supplied information.
After theta is updated to theta-prime, better performance under L-hat is expressed as an expectation.
Loss is treated as lower-is-better, whereas reward in reinforcement learning is usually higher-is-better.
Proposer creates questions; solver solves; verifier checks correctness; the loop is described as requiring almost no human intervention.
The lecturer says some recent work reports benefits from extra textbook or example information for the proposer. The individual methods and experimental limits must be checked in their source papers.

The manual-labelled caption uses a Chinese term that differs from the technological singularity terminology printed on page 2. The original caption excerpt is preserved; the article should paraphrase the PDF concept without claiming independent audio transcription.
